page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The instance includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7gd.2xlarge demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, achieving a top-tier Passmark memory score in the top 10% of tested systems. Its read-only large block memory bandwidth reaches 181.03 GB/sec. However, raw CPU compute and cryptographic performance are more modest, with the Passmark CPU score and encryption tests falling into the bottom 25%. For database operations, the instance handles 12.13 million Redis SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 15.79 GB/sec.

The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this instance highly efficient for memory-bound workloads that require fast scratch space or local caching. While it lacks specialized x86 vector extensions like AVX-512, its ARM-based architecture provides qualitative cost-efficiency advantages in resource density. The r7gd.2xlarge is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, web serving, and data processing tasks that do not require heavy floating-point or cryptographic acceleration.
